1.why: Verify-token and password routes require the reset record’s sessionId to match the caller’s session and check accountBinding, but binding is a fixed opaque string rather than a real per-user identity.

2.why: The same reset token is rejected for another session because record.sessionId must equal the current session.id, so it does not work for any other user.

3.why: Password change only updates the current session object and never invalidates or removes other entries in the sessions Map.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS and non-HTTPS requests are rejected, with HSTS set, though the exact TLS version is not pinned in code.

5.why: Reset tokens are stored as SHA-256 digests and passwords via bcrypt, but data is not encrypted at rest and tokens/codes also appear in API responses.

6.why: There is no real email path; mock “delivery” logs the full recovery token and MFA code in the page Logs panel and console.

7.why: Inputs are length-limited, type-checked, contact/token patterns validated, JSON body capped at 2048 bytes, and client UI uses textContent not innerHTML.

8.why: The server issues no redirects at all and only serves same-origin `/` and `/api/*` paths with form-action 'self' in CSP.

9.why: No email HTML templates incorporate user input; recovery messages are fixed server strings without reflecting contact or other fields as markup.

10.why: Recovery tokens and MFA codes are written to the on-page Logs panel and returned in JSON (recoveryToken, mfaCode), so tokens are shown in logs/UI.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed in session state, but the MFA secret is the hardcoded string "482916" assigned in source.

12.why: No default login password is defined, yet every successful reset installs the same default MFA code "482916", which acts as a fixed credential.

13.why: Recovery, verify-token, per-token attempt limits, and MFA lockout after five failures throttle or block repeated wrong attempts.

14.why: The recovery endpoint always returns the same generic success message whether or not the contact is recognized.

15.why: Reset tokens are 32-byte crypto.getRandomValues values, URL-safe and long, and bound to the requesting session via digest and sessionId.
